transcript:
Header: 2026-08-03 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~46 minutes | Recording: yes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Hannah Lee (Redwood CSM); Maya Chen (Orchid CTO), Luis Ortega (Lead ML), Priya Nair (Product), Ethan Park (Infra)

Summary (auto): quick discovery - customer evaluating Redwood for API-powered product features, wants fastest path to a first inference in prod-like conditions.

[00:00] Samira (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro round? I'm Samira, AE on the account; Diego will cover the technical bits.
[00:12] Maya (Orchid): Hi all, Maya here. We're evaluating vendors to power a new in-app assistant. Main constraints: sub-200ms median latency for short queries, data residency in us-east, and encrypted customer PII at rest.
[00:28] Luis (Orchid): Also want clarity on cost — we expect bursty traffic, so curious about free credits and sample billing for first 100k tokens.
[00:40] Samira: Great — those are exactly the things Redwood helps teams reason about. Quick look: we have a PLG quickstart with free credits so you can get to a first inference within an hour typically, assuming no infra outbound restrictions. Diego, want to give a quick overview of hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
[00:56] Diego (Redwood SE): Yup. Hosted is fastest to start — our public API, you get SDKs, streaming, and out-of-the-box model catalog. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools, predictable p99 latency and isolation, and Private (VPC/on-prem) gives the full control for regulated workloads with customer-managed network. Important tradeoffs: Hosted = lowest time-to-first-token but shared infra; Dedicated = more predictable latency/cost at scale; Private = full control but longer lead time and infra engineering.
[01:25] Ethan (Orchid): When you say "time-to-first-token in an hour" — what are the steps concretely?
[01:33] Diego: Steps: 1) Sign up + apply credits, 2) add API key and run the quickstart curl, 3) optionally mount your model config or pin a curated open model, 4) run a small benchmark to see median/99p latency. If you keep networking open to Redwood endpoints it's straightforward — otherwise Private requires VPC setup and a customer-controlled control plane which takes longer.
[01:58] Priya (Orchid): Do you provide a playbook for infra teams? Our infra folks will ask about firewall rules and egress.
[02:05] Hannah (Redwood CSM): Yes — we have a checklist: allowed IP ranges, SNI, TLS cert expectations, and a step-by-step 'time-to-first-inference' checklist. I'll attach that.
[02:16] Luis: Cool. On pricing — the free credits are for PLG usage, but how do you demonstrate likely monthly costs? Want to model tokens per feature.
[02:24] Samira: We'll send a simple calc sheet. It shows tokens per message assumptions; we also include batching and caching levers. For an initial pilot we often recommend Hosted with a small Dedicated pool as you ramp.
[02:36] Maya: Security: does Redwood support KMS or HSM? We need encryption keys under our control.
[02:41] Diego: For Private deployments we support customer KMS integration and HSM on-prem patterns. For Dedicated and Hosted we offer envelope encryption and an enterprise KMS integration path. We also produce audit logs and can integrate with your SIEM via syslog.
[03:02] Ethan: SSO and RBAC?
[03:05] Samira: SAML/SSO is supported for Console access, RBAC is role-based and we can map to your IdP groups. There's also token scoping per-route for application calls.
[03:18] Luis: Latency: you mentioned p99 SLA for Dedicated. What numbers should we expect for a 2k context?
[03:25] Diego: p50 p99 depends heavily on model size and batching. For a medium-sized open model under our optimized runtime we've seen p50 ~ 80-120ms and p99 under 400ms on Dedicated tuned instances. Hosted will vary more but we can run a benchmark with your sample payloads to get empirical numbers.
[03:46] Priya: Is quantization supported to lower cost?
[03:49] Diego: Yes — our runtime supports quantized variants and we can recommend a quantization profile depending on your quality tolerance. There's tradeoff docs we'll link.
[03:59] Maya: What about caching? We need certain prompts to be cached for cost. Is prefix/KV cache automatic?
[04:05] Diego: We have automatic prefix caching and KV cache behavior, but semantics differ by model. We'll show how to configure TTLs and cache keys in the console. Sometimes the transcription shows as "KV cash" in logs, so FYI that phrase crops up.
[04:20] Samira: Let's talk about the pilot scope — what would success look like for Orchid?
[04:25] Priya: Product goal is <200ms median for our top-10 intents, cost under $X per 1k queries (we'll share exact target), and no PII leaving our control for certain flows.
[04:36] Maya: Also need to validate data residency and a contract for logs retention.
[04:40] Samira: Sounds good. For PII we can recommend a hybrid approach: keep sensitive routing to Private or Dedicated with customer KMS, use Hosted for non-sensitive queries while you validate.
[04:52] Luis: Any big blockers for us to hit first inference in an hour?
[04:56] Diego: Typically network restrictions or IdP setup slow things down. If infra can allow egress to Redwood endpoints and a person can run curl we do the rest. We'll provide the quickstart scripts that run in CI or locally.
[05:08] Maya: We'd like to run a small latency benchmark — Diego, you mentioned a spreadsheet. What would you need from us?
[05:14] Diego: Sample payloads (JSON request examples), expected concurrency/QPS, desired sequence lengths, and whether you want context windows preserved. If you can share a small test corpus we'll run both Hosted and Dedicated variants and return p50/p95/p99 and cost per token estimates.
[05:30] Priya: timeline wise we want pilot live within 2 weeks if possible.
[05:33] Samira: We're confident — Hosted pilot can be live in 1-3 days with free credits; Dedicated pilot depends on sizing but can be in 1-2 weeks with reserved capacity. Private is the longest (several weeks to months).
[05:47] Ethan: Regarding compliance: do you have SOC2 documentation and pen test reports we can share with legal?
[05:52] Hannah: Yes, we'll share our security package (SOC2, ISO summary, pen test redacted exec summary) and our data handling policies. We'll also include how audit logs are surfaced.
[06:03] Maya: Good. Any hidden costs like egress or storage?
[06:07] Samira: Storage for KV cache is typically included. Egress to your app is the usual network egress from cloud provider — no Redwood-specific surcharge beyond API usage. We will call out any add-ons (long-term observability retention, premium SLAs).
[06:22] Luis: Competitors we looked at had tricky onboarding — long config windows. How does Redwood's SDKs look?
[06:28] Diego: We have SDKs in major languages, examples for serverless, mobile, and edge. Also a one-click quickstart repo that runs tests against our hosted endpoint.
[06:38] Maya: Ok let's talk scale — our plan is to go from pilot to 100k active monthly users over 6 months. How do you recommend we migrate from Hosted to Dedicated?
[06:47] Samira: Two paths: 1) Run pilot on Hosted, monitor cost/latency. When you hit predictable load we provision Dedicated capacity — migration is mostly config change and pinning model versions. 2) If you need strict isolation early, start on Dedicated for predictable p99 and capacity planning. We generally prefer the former for speed.
[07:05] Priya: Any constraints on model choices?
[07:07] Diego: We host a curated catalog (open models) and also support customer models for Private/Dedicated. For Hosted you can pick from the catalog; for Dedicated/Private we can pull containerized model artifacts.
[07:20] Luis: About observability — can we get token-level cost and per-route latency?
[07:25] Hannah: Yes, Console includes per-route dashboards, token cost breakdowns, traces and error rates. We can also hook into your datadog or prometheus via exporters.
[07:38] Maya: For the benchmark, can you also show effect of batching? We expect bursty traffic so batching might hurt latency.
[07:44] Diego: We'll run variants: no-batching, small-batch, and our continuous-batching setup. We'll include latency/cost tradeoffs. Batching helps cost but increases tail latency.
[07:58] Samira: Quick question: are you planning to use Redwood embeddings too? We have combined cost models for generation + embeddings.
[08:03] Priya: Possibly for retrieval — we'll discuss after pilot.
[08:07] Maya: Ok, can you repeat the exact artifacts you'll share after this call?
[08:10] Samira: Sure — 1) Quickstart playbook and checklist, 2) pricing worksheet and sample calc, 3) security package (SOC2/ISO/pen test summary), 4) SE benchmark template and instructions. Diego will run the benchmark and share results.
[08:22] Luis: Great. Any red flags on our side that would make Hosted impossible?
[08:26] Diego: Only if you must keep sensitive prompts entirely on-prem or have strict network air-gap rules. Otherwise Hosted works for most initial pilots.
[08:35] Priya: Who owns the pilot onboarding? Who will be our point of contact?
[08:38] Samira: I'll be your AE. Diego will lead the tech bench and Hannah will support onboarding and coordinate security paperwork. We'll set a 1:1 for the bench handoff.
[08:48] Maya: Cool. Let's lock a follow-up tech deep dive — week of Aug 10 works.
[08:53] Samira: I'll send calendar invites. Anything else?
[08:56] Ethan: One last infra question — do you have advisory on VPC peering vs private endpoints for Dedicated?
[09:01] Diego: Yes, we'll include guidance. Private endpoints via VPC endpoints gives better security and simpler routing but peering can work depending on your topology.
[09:12] Samira: Alright thanks everyone. We'll share materials and next steps.
[09:17] Maya: Thanks, appreciate it.
